trees.name: Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei

location.address: Rua Jorge Amado, Aldeamento Turistico de Pedras d'el Rei, Santa Luzia, Tavira

trees.pin_source: Commons photographer's geotag at the trunk (Vitor Oliveira, 2025-07-10), five geotagged files within 18 m of the ICNF coordinate
trees.story:
Tavira's own tourist route sends you past a holiday resort's reception desk to see this olive. Portugal classified it a Tree of Public Interest in 1984, and when the forest service measured it in 2006 the trunk was 7.74 metres round and the tree 10.3 metres tall. The register gave it an age of 2,210 years.

Read that number as a claim. The register and the 2021 Tree of the Year nomination both put it near two thousand years, and tree bloggers who visited in 2007 repeated a carbon-dating figure of about 2,000 without saying who did the dating. No ring count or published study has turned up. Somewhere between one and two thousand years is the honest version, and even the low end makes it older than the kingdom of Portugal.

The trunk is hollow and split into separate limbs, with a gap between two of them wide enough to look inside. Nominated for Portugal's Tree of the Year in 2022, it stands among the low white houses of the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village at Santa Luzia, a few kilometres southwest of Tavira. The municipal route gives the directions. Pass the reception, take the second street on the left, the Rua Jorge Amado, and it is about 25 metres along on the left. A second large olive grows nearby, unclassified and unmeasured since a 2007 visit put it near six metres round.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the hollow trunk, 7.74 metres round and split into several limbs. It stands about 25 metres along the Rua Jorge Amado, on the left, the second street left after the resort reception.

official_register.name: ICNF Arvoredo de Interesse Publico KNJ1/195

trees.access: Inside the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village (aldeamento turistico) at Santa Luzia. Tavira municipality's own route 'Os segredos e encantos da Ria Formosa' sends visitors past the resort reception to the tree on the Rua Jorge Amado; no fee is mentioned.
trees.transport: A few kilometres southwest of Tavira's centre by road, past Santa Luzia; the municipal route reaches it by car on the CM1347.

trees.name: Blue gums of the Centro de Saude

location.address: East side of the Estrada de Saboia (EN 266), opposite the Centro de Saude, Monchique

trees.pin_source: OpenStreetMap natural=tree node 6471090226 'Eucalipto do Centro de Saude' (the 37 m tree of the pair)
trees.story:
The larger of these two blue gums was 40 metres tall when it was measured in 2010, with a trunk 6.1 metres round at chest height. Its neighbour reached 37.6 metres and 4.9 metres round. There used to be three. On 26 January 2013, a week after storms swept across Portugal, one of the group came down. The Via Algarviana's guide to Monchique's monumental trees says the two bigger ones came through and were put forward for classification as Trees of Public Interest. That classification has not been granted so far as we can find.

They are an awkward kind of monument. Blue gums come from southern Victoria and Tasmania, and arrived in Portugal in the nineteenth century. The same guide counts 68 percent of Monchique's municipality as forest, and 80 percent of that forest as eucalyptus, much of it planted for paper pulp. Against that background, a pair grown to 40 metres beside a village road is a different thing to stand under.

They stand on the east side of the Estrada de Saboia at the edge of the village, where the road leaves for Saboia and Lisbon, opposite the Centro de Saude. The health centre's garden across the road holds camellias and hydrangeas. Nobody has published an age for them, and we have no recent photograph. If you pass, a picture would tell us both are still standing.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise them by their height, the larger 40 metres tall with a trunk 6.1 metres round. They stand on the east side of the Estrada de Saboia, opposite the Centro de Saude, where the road leaves the village.
trees.access: Beside the public road at the village exit towards Saboia, opposite the health centre; seen from the pavement, free.
trees.transport: At the edge of Monchique village, about ten minutes on foot from the Largo de Sao Sebastiao; the bus from Portimao to Monchique takes 40 to 50 minutes.
trees.verify_notes: Single written source (Via Algarviana 'Rota das Arvores Monumentais' guide, Arvores da Vila circuit, tree 2, measured 2010) plus an OpenStreetMap node tagged natural_monument (v2 edited 2026-05-23). Not on ICNF's classified list (KML fetched 2026-11-02). Alive not independently dated; stated on the page. Ensemble of two side by side, one place to stand. Ten minutes on foot from the Largo de Sao Sebastiao is derived from the distance (about 650 m by road) and stated loosely.

tavira.intro: Tavira's great tree is the Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei, an olive classified as a Tree of Public Interest in 1984, with a hollow trunk 7.74 metres round. Portugal's forest service registers its age at more than two thousand years, a figure nobody has tested. It stands in the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village at Santa Luzia, a few kilometres southwest of the town, and Tavira's own tourist route sends visitors to it.
tavira.meta_description: The Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei near Tavira, an olive classified in 1984 with a hollow trunk 7.74 metres round.
tavira.question_meta: Tavira's mapped tree is the Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei, a classified olive at Santa Luzia that its register calls about two thousand years old.
tavira.question_answer: The tree mapped in Tavira is the Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei, an olive at Santa Luzia classified as a Tree of Public Interest in 1984. Portugal's forest service measured its trunk at 7.74 metres round in 2006 and gave it an age of 2,210 years, a claim nobody has dated.
tavira.question_context: The Oliveira Real is on the national register of Trees of Public Interest kept by the ICNF, Portugal's forest service, classified on 2 August 1984. Its 2006 measurement gives 10.3 metres of height and a trunk 7.74 metres round; a 2007 visit by tree bloggers measured 7.8 metres, and the Tree of the Year nomination quotes 11 metres of perimeter, probably taken lower down. The age of 2,210 years is the register's figure and the nomination repeats it, but no ring count or published dating study supports it, so read it as somewhere between one and two thousand years. It was a candidate for Portugal's Tree of the Year in 2022. The trunk is hollow, split into several limbs. It stands on the Rua Jorge Amado inside the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village at Santa Luzia; Tavira municipality's route 'Os segredos e encantos da Ria Formosa' tells visitors to pass the reception, take the second street on the left and look left after about 25 metres. A second large olive, unclassified, grows nearby.

monchique.intro: Monchique maps four trees: a plane 41 metres tall beside a watermill in the Barranco dos Pisoes, a Norfolk Island pine of 36.5 metres on the terrace of the municipal park, a Monchique oak, a species critically endangered in Portugal, on the EN 267 towards Alferce, and a pair of blue gums 40 metres tall opposite the health centre. The village sits high in the Serra de Monchique, about an hour and a half from Lagos by bus with a change in Portimao.
monchique.meta_description: Four big trees in Monchique, Algarve: a 41-metre plane by a mill, a Norfolk Island pine, a rare Monchique oak and two 40-metre blue gums.
monchique.question_meta: Monchique's mapped trees are a 41-metre plane by a mill, a Norfolk Island pine, a rare Monchique oak and a pair of 40-metre blue gums.
monchique.question_answer: Monchique's mapped trees are three Trees of Public Interest, the Barranco dos Pisoes plane, 41 metres tall and classified in 1947, the Norfolk Island pine of the Quinta da Vila and a Monchique oak beside the EN 267, plus a pair of blue gums 40 metres tall opposite the health centre. The forest service gave the first three an age of about 150 years in 2006.
monchique.question_context: Three of the four are on the national register of Trees of Public Interest kept by the ICNF, Portugal's forest service, and on the town's own list. The plane was protected first, in 1947, the pine and the oak in 1993. The plane stands at the entrance to the Barranco dos Pisoes leisure area beside the Poucochinho mill, on the PR4 Trilho dos Moinhos walk about two kilometres from the centre. The araucaria rises over a small terrace of the Parque Municipal and is visible from across the village; a second, taller classified araucaria at the Quinta do Viador is a different tree. The oak is a Quercus canariensis, which in Portugal grows wild only in the Serra de Monchique and the Mira basin, and it is a roadside view on a national road with no footpath. The blue gums, measured in 2010 at 40 and 37.6 metres, stand on the Estrada de Saboia at the edge of the village and are not classified. Monchique is reached by bus from Portimao in about 40 to 50 minutes, and from Lagos in about an hour and a half with a change in Portimao.
